title: Network's QR code is draggable, but dragging it to Dolphin or desktop does nothing
line: Dragging a Wi-Fi network's QR code onto the desktop or into Dolphin now drops a PNG file named after the network.
explanation: The QR code page started a drag with only raw image/png data. The desktop has no file drop for raw data, so it handed the bytes to a new Media Frame, which treated them as a path and stayed empty (the reporter's '[object Object]' KIO error). Dolphin on current master asks for a name and saves 'pasted file.png'. The change also saves the grabbed image as '<SSID>.png' (slashes replaced) in the user's runtime directory and adds it as text/uri-list, so drop targets get a normal file: Copy Here on the desktop or in Dolphin, and Media Frame or Set Image show the QR code.

commits.message:
applet: Offer the dragged Wi-Fi QR code as a PNG file

Dragging the QR code only offered raw image data, so the desktop turned
it into an empty Media Frame. The grabbed image is now also saved as a
PNG in the runtime directory and offered as a file URL to drop targets.

BUG: 509734

media.caption: Before: dropping the QR code on the desktop creates an empty Media Frame
After: the same drop offers the normal file menu; Copy Here puts HomeNet.png on the desktop
Before: in Dolphin it asks for a name first and saves 'pasted file.png'
After: in Dolphin Copy Here saves HomeNet.png directly

review.text: Saving the grabbed Wi-Fi QR code into the user-private XDG_RUNTIME_DIR and offering it via text/uri-list alongside image/png cleanly fixes both the empty Media Frame / '[object Object]' error on the desktop and the generic filename prompt in Dolphin. Using RuntimeLocation instead of a world-readable temp directory is a good security choice since the QR code encodes the Wi-Fi password, and replacing slashes plus percent-encoding handles special SSID characters safely. Screenshots and verification notes match the diff and prove the fix.
